initial_draught.note: 30 ft 9 in forward and 33 ft 9 in aft at the time of the collision: Wilding's 1912 working estimate, used by Hackett and Bedford and by Halpern. The ship was thus trimmed about 0.2° by the stern.

waterline_pivot.note: While the trim stays below about 10°, the waterline appears to rotate about a fixed point of the original waterline 578 to 590 ft aft of the forward perpendicular; Halpern uses 585 ft. The Hackett and Bedford condition C7 (16.25° of trim) remains consistent with it. Fitch, Layton and Wormstedt argue that the point moves aft once boiler room 5 floods.

alternatives.holder: Tad Fitch, J. Kent Layton and Bill Wormstedt (as reported by Halpern)
alternatives.position: The pivot point moves aft after boiler room 5 has flooded.

trim.note: Intact condition: 3 ft by the stern over 850 ft.

trim.note: The Marine Forensics Panel places the first structural failure at a trim of about 15 to 17°; the mid-value is taken at the time the lights went out. No measured trim exists after 2:15.

heel.note: No list was reported at the moment of impact. Halpern assumes a slight pre-existing port list of about 2° and notes that using zero barely changes his curve.
Wheelhouse inclinometer five to ten minutes after impact (Hichens); 5.15° by Halpern's heeling-moment calculation.

Boat 8 cleared the side (Crawford); slight starboard list at boat 1 (Symons).
"She was not listing at all" when boat 9 reached the water (Ward).
Halpern's trend line; a port list was noted at boat 14.
Halpern's trend line (3½ to 4° to port); boats 13 and 15 lay against the starboard side.

The value shown is the one common to the published ranges: about 10° to port for Fitch, Layton and Wormstedt and for Halpern in 2017, and the lower bound of Halpern's 2026 range.
